correctness.rationale: The ellipse support integral gives the exact smooth perimeter function. Its two strictly negative spectral derivatives exclude all critical normals except six principal axes. Direct principal-plane tilts give the stated positive Hessian factors; the coarea/Morse calculation includes both antipodal saddles and checks the sphere probability normalization. The endpoint constants follow from Gaussian quadratic area integrals. A standalone verifier independently constructs restricted forms and checks Hessian coefficients for three triaxial axis triples.

value.rationale: A natural measured central-section circumference has a qualitatively distinct density fingerprint: two finite nonzero endpoint densities and a unique explicit logarithmic interior divergence whose location singles out the extreme-axis section. The coefficient depends on both axis gaps and ellipse-perimeter derivatives, a nontrivial shape-sensitive invariant. This goes beyond an ordinary pushforward exercise because the complete global critical-point classification and all three local coefficients are explicitly resolved.
